market_question: Iran closes its airspace by June 30?
reasoning: Over the past two years, Iran has executed two major, non-weather airspace closures (Apr 2024, Jan 2026), roughly one per year. Over the next ~3 months, the base-rate probability of another such closure is around 25‑30%. While regional tensions remain elevated, the market’s 57% implied probability appears too high absent a clear imminent trigger. Given the 17-point gap, the "No" side is undervalued.
evidence_points: Historical frequency of major closures is ~1 per 12 months, implying a ~25% chance in any 3-month window.
The January 2026 closure already reflected peak retaliation; subsequent de‑escalation phases tend to follow such events.
No new flashpoint (e.g., large-scale strike) has emerged that would make another closure highly likely before June 30.
sources_consulted: General background on Iran-Israel military tensions
